subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should claude-cli native or Workflow-backed background work be explicitly refused unless it uses OpenClaw task infrastructure, or should OpenClaw support it by hosting/detaching workers with durable origin and completion delivery?
rationale: Both choices are product/runtime contracts with user-visible compatibility consequences; source inspection cannot safely choose whether to expose native Claude longwork, deny it, or build a durable bridge.

options.title: Deny unsupported native longwork by default
options.body: Keep native Claude background Bash/Monitor denied, add any missing Workflow/native affordance denial or docs, and direct users to OpenClaw tasks, Task Flow, cron, ACP, or sessions_spawn for durable longwork.

options.title: Support native longwork with a bridge
options.body: Design and implement a durable host or detached worker contract that snapshots origin, persists completion, and proves delivery across turn boundaries and gateway restarts.

options.title: Defer pending live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open without product action until a maintainer-run Claude CLI Workflow reproduction shows which remaining native surfaces are still exposed and failing.

recommendation.title: Deny unsupported native longwork by default
recommendation.body: Keep native Claude background Bash/Monitor denied, add any missing Workflow/native affordance denial or docs, and direct users to OpenClaw tasks, Task Flow, cron, ACP, or sessions_spawn for durable longwork.

likelyOwner.reason: The live Claude CLI session lifecycle work is the central runtime boundary for deciding whether native longwork can be safely hosted.
